name: Trace Assembly Program Execution
recognitionClueHinglish: Ek assembly language program diya hai aur poocha hai final register/memory VALUE kya hoga, ya program kya COMPUTE karta hai — is topic ka sabse bada pattern hai (21 me se 14 PYQs).
whatShouldComeToMind: Maintain an explicit table of register and relevant memory values, update after EVERY instruction.
Read each instruction's semantics carefully (given as comments/documentation in the question) before tracing — don't assume standard meaning without checking.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. List all registers/memory locations involved with their initial values.
2. Process each instruction in order, updating the table exactly per its documented semantics.
variationsObserved: Data-forwarding optimization questions — identify which instruction sequence can be shortened by bypassing memory round-trips.
Latency-table-based dependency questions — track WHEN a value becomes available (not just what it becomes) for pipelined/dependent instruction sequences.
commonTraps: Misreading a hypothetical processor's custom instruction semantics (they often differ from standard x86/ARM conventions) — always use the EXACT semantics given in the question, never assume.

name: Instruction Encoding / Bit-Field Sizing
recognitionClueHinglish: Poocha hai ek fixed-width instruction word me OPCODE, REGISTER operands, aur IMMEDIATE operand ke liye kitne bits allocate honge, ya kaunsa PC value legal hai — ye bit-arithmetic pattern hai.
whatShouldComeToMind: opcode bits = ⌈log2(#instructions)⌉. register field bits = ⌈log2(#registers)⌉ per operand.
Immediate bits = total width − opcode bits − (register bits × number of register operands).
PC legality: must be aligned to instruction-size boundaries from the program's start address.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Compute opcode bits and register-field bits using the ceiling-log2 formulas.
2. Subtract from total instruction width to find remaining bits for the immediate operand.
3. For PC legality, check the candidate address is start_address + k×(instruction size in bytes) for some integer k≥0.
commonTraps: Forgetting to account for MULTIPLE register-operand fields (subtracting only once when an instruction has 2 or 3 register operands).

name: Clock Cycles / Timing Analysis
recognitionClueHinglish: Poocha hai program execute karne me KITNE clock cycles lagenge, given per-instruction cycle costs (aur shayad loops/latencies) — ye timing-summation pattern hai.
whatShouldComeToMind: Sum (cycles per instruction type × execution count) — carefully account for LOOP repetitions, not just static instruction count.
For latency-dependency questions, track when a value becomes AVAILABLE for the next dependent instruction, not just when the producing instruction issues.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Identify each instruction's cycle cost from the given table.
2. Determine how many times each instruction actually executes (accounting for loop bodies running multiple times).
3. Sum up total cycles = Σ(cost × execution count).
commonTraps: Counting loop-body instructions only ONCE instead of accounting for all iterations.

name: Conceptual Properties (privileged instructions, addressing modes, stack behavior)
recognitionClueHinglish: Poocha hai ek instruction (jaise RFE) PRIVILEGED hai ya nahi, ya specific addressing-mode notation ((X)+, -(X)) ka matlab kya hai, ya stack pointer behavior — ye definitional/conceptual pattern hai.
whatShouldComeToMind: Instructions that affect processor MODE or handle exceptions (like RFE) are typically PRIVILEGED (kernel-mode only).
(X)+ = auto-increment AFTER use (forward traversal); -(X) = auto-decrement BEFORE use (stack push style, or reverse traversal).
generalSolvingApproach: 1. For privilege questions, reason about whether the instruction could compromise system integrity if available to user programs — exception-handling and mode-switching instructions are privileged.
2. For addressing-mode notation questions, apply the standard convention directly (+ after = increment-after-use; - before = decrement-before-use).
commonTraps: Confusing which addressing mode increments/decrements BEFORE vs AFTER the memory access.
